olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Find the least real number $c$ such that, for every integer $n\ge3$ and every set of positive real numbers
$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n,$$
there exists a label assignment of the vertices of a regular $n$-gon by the numbers
$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$
so that, for every edge of the $n$-gon, the ratio of the larger label to the smaller label on the endpoints of that edge is at most $c$.
figure_description: Optimization problem on labeling the vertices of a regular polygon.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
In acute triangle $ABC$, points $A_1,B_1,C_1$ lie on sides $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points such that
$$PA_1\parallel QB_1$$
and
$$PB_1\parallel QC_1.$$
Suppose that points
$$P,A_1,B_1,Q,C_1$$
all lie on one circle. Prove that if lines $PA, QB,$ and $C_1A_1$ are concurrent, then lines $QA, PC,$ and $A_1B_1$ are concurrent.
figure_description: Triangle with cevian points and cyclic/concurrency conditions.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Suppose that $n$ and $k$ are positive integers such that
$$
k-\sqrt{k^2-n}
$$
is rational. Prove that there exists a divisor $d$ of $n$ such that
$$d+\frac nd$$
is rational and less than $2k$.
statement_note: Radical expression visually verified from official PDF because OCR partially corrupted square-root notation. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

statement:
Convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ satisfies
$$AB\cdot CD=BC\cdot DA.$$
Point $X$ lies inside quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that
$$\angle XAB=\angle XCD$$
and
$$\angle XBC=\angle XDA.$$
Prove that
$$\angle BXA+\angle DXC=180^\circ.$$
figure_description: Convex quadrilateral with equal-angle conditions and interior point.

statement: A social network has $2019$ users, some pairs of whom are friends. Users can communicate by private messages. If one user sends a private message to another, then neither the sender nor the recipient can send a private message to any of their friends for the next minute. Determine the maximum possible number of private messages that can be sent each minute.
figure_description: Optimization problem on message sending in a friendship graph.

statement:
Find all infinite sequences
$$a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$$
of positive integers for which there exists an integer $N>0$ such that for all
$$n\ge N,$$
$$
\frac{a_1}{a_2}+ rac{a_2}{a_3}+\cdots+\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}+ rac{a_n}{a_1}
$$
is an integer.
statement_note: Cyclic sum notation visually verified from official PDF because OCR partially corrupted fraction formatting. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
